`reuse_verdict` checks that the prior artifact's head is an ancestor of the supplied `head_sha`, that only store paths changed between them, and that the working tree is clean. It never checks that `head_sha` is the repository's actual HEAD. A caller passing an older `head_sha` while HEAD carries later product commits gets "reused", because cleanliness is judged against HEAD. This weakens "changed code invalidates it".

The facade's live-state refusal covers only request and policy inputs (`_INPUTS`) plus `--out`. `--project-root`, `--artifact` and `--log` are not checked. Writes under the project-management store are still refused by `log_sink_refusal.refuse`, but the facade does not itself refuse a `--project-root` inside `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot`. The verification argv would run with that directory as cwd.

The new pre-run symlink-dirt test accepts either refusal or execution producing non-reusable evidence, although the contract requires refusal before spawning. Assert the dirty-tree refusal and use a spawn marker to prove the command never runs.
